title: Euthyne
description: Accountability for AI agents: what each agent was allowed to do next to what it did, signed and checkable by anyone. Starting with coding agents.
longDescription: AI agents act for people, and the record of what they did usually belongs to whoever ran them. Euthyne keeps a record an outsider can check. It starts with coding agents. The CLI hooks into Claude Code, captures the agent's permission settings at the start of a session as a signed mandate, and signs a receipt on the developer's machine for every tool call, marked inside, outside or unknown against that mandate. Content is kept as salted hashes. Receipts go into a public append-only log with signed checkpoints and OpenTimestamps proofs, and anyone can verify them on euthyne.com/verify or offline, without an account. I'm building it on my own.

title: Verana Cross-Ecosystem Wallet Interop
description: Live trust-registry resolution wired into third-party identity wallets and solutions, replacing their hardcoded issuer lists.
longDescription: Every mature identity wallet ships a static list of trusted issuers, compiled at build time and updated by release. This work replaces that list with a live, fail-closed call to the Verana trust resolver, using the same HTTP surface in every target so the approach is portable rather than bespoke. Shipped and device-verified: MOSIP's Inji as a full issuer, wallet and verifier triangle; the EUDI reference Android wallet validated on testnet against France Identité's Unfold playground; Talao AltMe, Sphereon, Paradym and Procivis One built and demonstrated on device with both trusted and rogue paths verified; and Hologram running natively on vs-agent. SWIYU, the Swiss Confederation wallet, is partial: positive and control issuance flows are accepted on Android, one verifier request path remains blocked. Built for the Global Digital Trust Collaboration Award 2026 and shown at GDC Geneva in September 2026.

title: Hologram Verifiable Service Agents
description: DIDComm and verifiable-credential AI agents running as production services on 2060.io's Hologram.
longDescription: Hologram is 2060.io's verifiable-trust messaging platform, where every connection between a human and an agent is gated by DIDs and verifiable credentials. I built and shipped several agents on it: a live-avatar agent backed by LiveKit that opens a session on connect, a multilingual concierge handling structured travel workflows, and a credential-gated automation bot. All are NestJS services deployed to Kubernetes with Helm, running on the vs-agent framework.

title: CiteMe
description: Generative engine optimization platform measuring how often AI search engines cite a brand.
longDescription: Search is moving from Google to AI answer engines. CiteMe crawls a site, runs multi-provider audits across the major AI engines, and returns a 0 to 100 score with prioritized, actionable fixes. A tracker surfaces real AI-bot visits so customers see which engines are reading their content. I co-founded it and serve as CIO, owning data, backend direction and infrastructure. Runs on Next.js 16, React 19, Supabase with pgvector for retrieval, a custom job queue, a multi-provider LLM layer, and Stripe billing.

title: Klyx
description: Web and AI studio for startups and tech teams: sites, AI audits, assistants and agents.
longDescription: Klyx is the studio I founded in Bordeaux. It started as a web studio and now does web and AI for startups and tech teams: an AI audit to find where it actually pays off, sites built to be read by both Google and AI engines, and assistants, agents and MCP servers shipped in two-week sprints on the client's own data. Clients talk directly to the person writing the code.

title: Hop Hop Immo
description: New-build property platform with Hoppy, a conversational AI assistant over 28,000+ homes.
longDescription: Hop Hop Immo is a Bordeaux platform for new-build homes, with a catalogue of 28,000+ properties. I built Hoppy, the conversational AI assistant live on the site that qualifies buyers and points them to matching homes. Beyond Hoppy I work across the Next.js site and its Java API: listing and programme pages, city pages, geo-search, financing simulators, user accounts and an in-house consent banner, plus the Python agent pipeline that writes content. I started as an intern in January 2026 and have been an apprentice there since September.

title: Parkour Bassin d'Arcachon
description: Website and member platform for PKBA, a parkour club near Arcachon I co-founded in 2025 and now preside.
longDescription: PKBA is a parkour club near Arcachon that I co-founded in 2025 and now preside, with more than 100 members. I designed and built its whole platform on my own: the public site, online sign-ups stored in Airtable, an admin dashboard to validate licences and export member data, holiday camp sign-ups, and live Stripe flows for the shop and donations. I trained as a competitive parkour athlete from 2017 to 2025, so this one is as personal as it is technical. The club has been featured by France 3 Nouvelle-Aquitaine.

title: VertiFlow
description: Parkour and urban-movement brand with a hand-built e-commerce storefront.
longDescription: VertiFlow is a parkour and urban-movement brand I founded, blending apparel, content and community to make the sport more accessible. I built and operate the entire storefront at vertiflow.fr from scratch: product catalogue, cart, checkout via serverless functions, promo codes and automated order emails, alongside the SEO blog, FAQ and full legal pages. Hand-coded and deployed on Netlify, and connected to the PKBA club ecosystem.

title: PkVision
description: Open experiment in recognising and scoring parkour tricks from video. In progress.
longDescription: PkVision tries to recognise parkour tricks in video and score them, because competitive parkour judging is subjective and judges disagree. It started with pose estimation and learned models. Right now I'm trying a simpler idea: count flips and twists from 2D keypoints with fixed rules, starting with the backflip family. Still in progress, no results to show yet.

title: Reciproq
description: Marketing site for a French mental health startup.
longDescription: Reciproq is a French startup working to improve access to mental health care. Over a two-month engagement I built key pages of its first marketing site in Next.js and Tailwind, implementing the Figma design system with a mobile-first, accessible and performance-minded approach, plus data-driven modules for testimonials and pricing so the team could update content without a deploy.
